PullRequest.Title: agentHost: prevent duplicate Codex skills across sessions
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

Stop registering client-synced plugin skill caches through the process-global `skills/extraRoots/set` API. Those caches are scoped by workspace and revision, so registering their union makes native discovery expose duplicate copies and skills from unrelated sessions.

Replace that delivery path with supported session-scoped behavior:

- Advertise the enabled client skills' names, descriptions, and synced file paths through `turn/start.additionalContext`. Send the current catalogue on every turn, including an explicit empty catalogue after removal.
- Grant read-only access to the session's skill directories through the existing thread permission profiles. Reuse start/resume reconciliation when the directories or permission profile change; preserve existing filesystem restrictions and profile inheritance.
- Keep native skill discovery, including `~/.agents/skills`, separate and unchanged. Do not register generated bundles in the global native catalogue.

The review identified a real gap in the original draft: `thread/resume` cannot update `selectedCapabilityRoots`, and the pinned SDK did not advertise client skills through that path. The revised implementation no longer relies on those roots for client skills. It also avoids `turn/start.permissions` while thread-specific read grants are active, because that field reloads the process-wide profile and drops those grants.

This uses the existing session lifecycle and the pinned SDK; it does not add a new manager, SDK upgrade, or cache migration.

## Validation

- Merged `origin/main` through `978cb41d811` and rebuilt the complete product successfully with the corresponding dependencies.
- **529 Codex unit tests pass.**
- **All 4 Codex provider integration tests pass** with the repository-pinned **Codex 0.149.1**, including the original failing CI assertion that plugin skills reach the actual model request.
- New integration coverage checks add/remove after the first turn, workspace isolation, native user skills, actual shell reads outside workspace/temp roots, read-grant preservation across permission changes, denied unrelated reads and skill writes, preserved workspace writes, and revocation while the cached file remains on disk.
- Launch + dap-cli verification in an isolated Code OSS Agents window with a real ChatGPT-backed Codex model: add one skill to an existing thread, read its body, disable it, and verify that both its current catalogue entry and read grant disappear without replacing the thread. Built-in client skills remain single entries.
- Targeted ESLint, hygiene, and `git diff --check` pass.

The fix takes effect when running the updated agent host; it does not retroactively rewrite skill listings already present in chat history.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The per-turn insertion, full-catalog serialization, normal send path, and persistence of older catalogs are all directly evidenced by changed source, changed subsystem documentation, and the integration-test request inspection. Exact latency depends on chat length and catalog size, which affects severity rather than mechanism confidence.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Serialized prompt bytes and model input tokens retained in thread history and transmitted/processed by subsequent model requests.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For S bytes of catalog and T turns, the Tth request can contain O(S*T) historical catalog bytes and the session cumulatively processes O(S*T^2) catalog bytes; S grows with enabled skill count and description/path lengths.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increasing network payload, token-processing latency, and context-window pressure over the lifetime of a chat.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Client skills were registered through `skills/extraRoots/set` when roots changed or a connection started; `turn/start` did not append a client-skill catalog to each turn's persisted conversation history.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every normal turn now adds a `vscode.clientSkills` application-context entry containing the entire current client-skill catalog, even when the catalog is empty or unchanged.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 5930 unconditionally inserts the full `clientSkillInstructions` value into `turn/start.additionalContext`; previously no per-turn client-skill context entry existed.
Findings.Title: Avoid appending the skill catalog on every turn
Findings.Impact: Long Codex chats repeatedly resend and reprocess unchanged skill metadata, increasing request bytes, input-token usage, and model latency; sufficiently long chats or large plugin catalogs reach the context limit earlier. This also affects sessions with no client skills because the empty-catalog block is still appended every turn.
Findings.Evidence: The changed `turn/start` payload unconditionally includes `currentCustomizationLaunch.clientSkillInstructions`. `codexClientSkillInstructions` serializes every model-invokable skill name, description, and absolute file path. The updated agent-host documentation explicitly states that every turn receives this catalog and that older catalogs can remain in conversation history; the provider integration test searches all developer-role input in a later model request and selects the last `<client_skills>` block, corroborating that these entries reach the model request history.
Findings.Recommendation: Track the last catalog/signature advertised for each backing thread and add this context only on the first turn and when the enabled catalog changes, including one explicit empty update for removal; reset that state only when a new thread/history requires it.

Scenarios.Scenario: Sending successive turns in a Codex chat with client skills enabled, disabled, or absent
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Before each normal `turn/start`, `_ensureCurrentLaunchBeforeTurn` rebuilds the current launch, then `turn/start` must complete before the turn progresses. The app-server incorporates `additionalContext` into the model request, so the newly added full skill catalog and all retained prior catalogs are on the model critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Discover workspace agents and workspace skills while rebuilding customization launch
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One pair of discovery operations per turn; cardinality scales with configured workspace roots.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same per-turn launch reconciliation performed workspace discovery before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Completes before `turn/start`; this discovery was already present and is not a diff-introduced regression.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send `turn/start` with the full client-skill catalog in `additionalContext`
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One IPC per turn; the added payload contains every enabled skill or an explicit empty catalog.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One `turn/start` IPC already occurred, but it did not carry a per-turn client-skill catalog.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The IPC must complete before asynchronous turn processing begins, and its context becomes model input.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: Transitive Codex app-server model request, corroborated by codexCustomizations.integrationTest.ts request capture
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send the assembled conversation, including retained application-context catalogs, to the model responses endpoint
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One or more model requests per turn; each later request can include every earlier catalog snapshot in thread history.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Client skills were registered through process-global extra roots, so no client-skill application message was appended to each turn's history.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Direct model-response critical path; larger token payload raises transfer and inference latency and consumes context.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Enabled model-invokable skill count and description/path length determine catalog size; chat turn count determines how many historical catalog snapshots can be retained. Even the empty catalog is appended once per turn.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Turns for a thread are issued sequentially; there is no coalescing or unchanged-catalog suppression. Each turn adds one catalog snapshot.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The parsed plugin store is reused, but the catalog string is rebuilt and appended every turn. No per-thread last-advertised signature suppresses unchanged catalogs; cold, warm, and empty catalogs all take the new path.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: unconditional per-turn insertion, full-catalog construction, normal-turn reachability, and historical persistence are directly evidenced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact token and latency growth depends on skill catalog size, turn count, provider history handling, and compaction frequency; the changed documentation and integration request inspection establish that older catalogs can persist and reach model input.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium-severity repeated prompt serialization: unchanged full or empty catalogs accumulate in history and increase later model-request cost.

Scenarios.Scenario: Adding, removing, or changing client-synced skills after a thread already has history
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Customization sync/copy and parsing complete first; reconciliation marks an existing materialized thread for reload when skill roots/profile change. The next turn resumes the thread before sending one new current-catalog application context.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Sync and parse client plugin bundles
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per changed client customization set, across the changed plugins rather than per chat turn.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Plugin bundles were already copied and parsed before computing process-global skill roots.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Precedes customization publication/reconciliation; existing behavior, not newly introduced by this diff.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Unsubscribe and resume a materialized thread with updated permission-profile filesystem roots
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one serialized reload per converged customization/profile state before a turn.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Skill-root changes already altered selected capability roots/signatures and triggered thread reconciliation; the diff changes the config/profile payload and removes the global roots update.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks the first turn after a relevant customization or permission change.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of client plugin revisions, enabled skills, and changed session permission profiles; effective roots are deduplicated absolute skill directories.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Customization reconciliation is serialized per session by a `Sequencer`; thread resume is awaited before the next turn, avoiding concurrent reload bursts.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Synced plugin files and parsed plugin state are retained by the per-session store. Signature comparison avoids resume when launch-relevant state is unchanged, but catalog advertisement itself has no unchanged-state suppression.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for call path and serialization; low evidence of harmful fan-out because signature checks and the per-session sequencer bound reload work.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Plugin revision frequency and catalog size vary, but reconciliation is bounded and serialized; no independent regression beyond the repeated catalog-history issue was established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: dynamic changes are serialized and reload only when launch state differs; the significant regression is the catalog copies retained per turn.

Scenarios.Scenario: Starting or reconnecting the shared Codex app-server and materializing sessions
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Connection startup no longer waits for `skills/extraRoots/set`; each session later sends one `thread/start` or `thread/resume` with its own permission-root config. Connection establishment remains required before thread operations.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Removed process-global `skills/extraRoots/set` request during connection startup and customization refresh
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Previously one request per process startup plus serialized requests after client customization changes/disposal; now zero.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Startup awaited a global skill-root IPC before publishing the connection ready.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The startup request was removed from the connection critical path, improving rather than regressing startup.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Start or resume each session thread with session-scoped permission profile overrides
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One thread IPC per materialization or required reload; config size scales with deduplicated skill directories for that session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Thread start/resume already occurred and carried selected capability roots; client skill roots were also registered globally.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before that session can send a turn; the boundary existed previously, with changed payload only.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of live sessions and enabled skill directories per session; read roots are deduplicated before serialization.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Connection startup is represented by one shared promise. Session materializations may proceed independently after readiness; no new process-global roots sequencer remains.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The live connection is reused. Per-session plugin state supplies current roots; no process-global skill-root cache is populated on reconnect.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that global startup IPC is removed and session thread payload changes are bounded.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Large per-session skill sets enlarge thread config, but no repository evidence establishes a realistic size causing a separate material regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: startup removes a blocking IPC, while session-scoped permission serialization does not have enough evidence for a separate actionable regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Model invocation of a selected client skill outside the workspace
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The model receives the catalog, then may issue a shell/file-reading tool call for the advertised SKILL.md. That subprocess/filesystem read is required only when a task matches a skill, not on every turn.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: Transitive Codex tool execution exercised by codexCustomizations.integrationTest.ts
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run shell/file tool to read the selected SKILL.md
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: On demand per selected skill/tool call, not per catalog entry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Codex native skill handling also read selected skill files on demand; this diff changes discovery/permission delivery rather than proving additional body reads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks the model step that needs the skill body.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the selected synced SKILL.md from its cache path
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One read per model-issued file command in the tested path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Client skills were discovered from registered extra roots and their bodies remained file-backed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required for the model to use that skill, but remains lazy.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of skills actually selected by the model, normally one matching skill per task; catalog construction includes all enabled skills but body reads are on demand.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Tool calls follow Codex turn execution and approval/sandbox sequencing; tests exercise one shell invocation, with no diff-added parallel fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Synced skill files remain on disk. Metadata is advertised each turn, but skill bodies are read lazily only on invocation; removal revokes read permission while the cached file remains.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that body reads are lazy and permission-scoped; no evidence of changed read fan-out.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual model skill-selection frequency is workload-dependent.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding: the expensive file boundary remains demand-driven rather than eager or per-catalog-item.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all nine changed files and relevant Codex lifecycle paths. Reported one introduced repeated-work regression: unconditional per-turn skill catalogs accumulate in conversation/model history, causing prompt bytes, token cost, and latency to grow with both skills and turns. No additional boundary-fanout, startup, cache-lifecycle, or subprocess regression met the evidence threshold.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
